title: Formal writing and the language of the media
objectives: I can read a Ukrainian news report or an official notice and say what was done and by whom, even when the text names the action with a verbal noun or a form in '-но' or '-то'.
I can turn a verb and its object into a verbal noun with the genitive, as in 'ухва́лення зако́ну', and turn it back into a plain verb when I retell a text.
I can use the prepositions of official style, 'відпові́дно до', 'згі́дно з', 'у зв’язку́ з', 'з мето́ю' and 'що́до', each with its case.
I can punctuate parenthetical words, and the clarifications that 'зокре́ма' and 'то́бто' introduce, as Ukrainian requires.
I can write a short formal summary with the standard forms 'бра́ти у́часть', 'протя́гом' and 'у ра́зі', and explain how 'стаття́', 'у зв’язку́' and 'грома́дянин' are spelled and said.

vocabulary.note: A text in a newspaper, a magazine or on a news site, and also an article of a law: 'стаття́ зако́ну'. The doubled 'тт' stays before an ending vowel ('статті́', 'статтю́', 'статте́ю'), but the genitive plural has no ending and a single 'т': 'стате́й'.

example.target: Окса́на чита́є статтю́ про нови́й зако́н.
example.source: Oksana is reading an article about the new law.

vocabulary.note: Genitive 'заголо́вка'. The 'о' before the last consonant drops out in every other form, as in 'відсо́ток', 'відсо́тка'. The word is built on 'голова́', head: the title stands at the head of a text.

example.target: Сем не зрозумі́в заголо́вок статті́.
example.source: Sam didn't understand the headline of the article.

vocabulary.note: 'Ухвалю́', 'ухва́лиш', 'ухва́лять': the stress moves to the stem after the 'я' form. The imperfective partner is 'ухва́лювати'. A parliament, a government or a council adopts a law, a reform or a decision with it. Its passive participle is 'ухва́лений', its form in '-но' 'ухва́лено', and its verbal noun 'ухва́лення'.

example.target: Депута́ти ухвали́ли нови́й зако́н.
example.source: The members of parliament passed a new law.

vocabulary.note: Genitive 'зако́ну', with the '-у' of most abstract nouns. A law on a subject takes 'про' with the accusative: 'зако́н про ви́бори', the election law.

example.target: Цей зако́н ухвали́ли мину́лого ро́ку.
example.source: This law was passed last year.

vocabulary.note: Genitive 'уря́ду'. The government in the narrow sense: the ministers who run the country, in Ukraine the Cabinet of Ministers. A parliament or a council, 'ра́да', is not 'уря́д'.

example.target: Уря́д пообіця́в нову́ рефо́рму.
example.source: The government promised a new reform.

vocabulary.note: Power over others, and the people who hold it, so one singular noun names all the officials of a city or a country: 'міська́ вла́да', the city authorities. The verb that agrees with it is singular.

example.target: Міська́ вла́да пообіця́ла відремонтува́ти міст.
example.source: The city authorities promised to repair the bridge.

vocabulary.note: Plural even for a single election, so its adjectives and verbs are plural: 'Ви́бори бу́дуть восени́.' Genitive 'ви́борів', locative 'у ви́борах'. 'Ви́бір', choice, is a different word with a singular.

example.target: Насту́пні ви́бори бу́дуть восени́.
example.source: The next election will be in the autumn.

vocabulary.note: An elected member of a parliament or of a council: 'наро́дний депута́т', a member of the national parliament, literally 'people's deputy', and 'депута́т міської́ ра́ди', a member of the city council. For a woman, 'депута́тка'.

example.target: Наш депута́т прийшо́в на зу́стріч із грома́дянами.
example.source: Our member of parliament came to a meeting with citizens.
example.source_literal: Our deputy came on meeting with citizens.

vocabulary.note: The plural drops '-ин': 'грома́дяни', genitive 'грома́дян'. A woman is 'грома́дянка'. The word comes from 'грома́да', a community.

example.target: Ко́жен грома́дянин мо́же писа́ти до міської́ ра́ди.
example.source: Every citizen can write to the city council.
example.source_literal: Every citizen can to-write to city council.

vocabulary.note: What is reformed follows in the genitive: 'рефо́рма тра́нспорту', a reform of transport. A government adopts a reform with 'ухвали́ти' and carries it out over years.

example.target: Рефо́рма тра́нспорту почне́ться насту́пного ро́ку.
example.source: The transport reform will begin next year.

vocabulary.note: The event follows 'у' with the locative: 'бра́ти у́часть у ви́борах'. 'Бра́ти' changes as usual ('беру́', 'бере́ш'), the noun 'у́часть', participation, never changes, and the perfective is 'взя́ти у́часть'. It is the standard form of formal writing and careful speech.

example.target: Окса́на ча́сто бере́ у́часть у студе́нтських конце́ртах.
example.source: Oksana often takes part in student concerts.

vocabulary.note: With the genitive. A compound preposition: the adverb 'відпові́дно', correspondingly, from the root of 'ві́дповідь', and 'до'. It cites the law, rule or decision that an action follows.

example.target: Відпові́дно до зако́ну зая́ву тре́ба запо́внити украї́нською.
example.source: Under the law, the application has to be filled in in Ukrainian.
example.source_literal: Correspondingly to law application needed to-fill-in by-Ukrainian.

vocabulary.note: With the instrumental. A compound preposition: the adverb 'згі́дно', in agreement, which shares its root with 'зго́да', agreement, and with 'пого́джуватися', and 'з', which follows the euphony rule: 'згі́дно з ро́зкладом', 'згі́дно із зако́ном'. It cites a document or a plan; for a person's words Ukrainian says 'за слова́ми'.

example.target: Згі́дно з ро́зкладом по́їзд приї́де о дев’я́тій.
example.source: According to the timetable, the train arrives at nine.
example.source_literal: In-agreement with timetable train will-arrive at ninth.

vocabulary.note: With the instrumental. Built from 'у', the locative of 'зв’язо́к', connection, and 'з'. Official notices give the reason for a change with it, whether the change is welcome or not: 'у зв’язку́ з ремо́нтом', due to repairs.

example.target: У зв’язку́ з ремо́нтом музе́й зачи́нено до тра́вня.
example.source: Due to renovation, the museum is closed until May.
example.source_literal: In connection with renovation museum closed until May.

vocabulary.note: With the genitive. It is 'з' with the instrumental of 'мета́', goal, and the genitive after it names what the goal is: 'з мето́ю навча́ння', for the purpose of study. Speech says the same with 'щоб' and an infinitive: 'щоб навча́тися'.

example.target: Сем приї́хав до Ки́єва з мето́ю навча́ння.
example.source: Sam came to Kyiv to study.
example.source_literal: Sam arrived to Kyiv with goal of-study.

vocabulary.note: With the genitive. 'Що' and 'до' fused into one word. It names the subject of a question, a decision or an opinion: 'пита́ння що́до ви́борів', a question about the election. Speech often says 'про' with the accusative instead.

example.target: Що́до ви́борів уря́д ще нічо́го не повідо́мив.
example.source: The government has not announced anything about the election yet.
example.source_literal: Regarding elections government still nothing not informed.

vocabulary.note: It introduces a clarification: one member of a group named just before. A comma stands before 'зокре́ма' and none after it.

example.target: Сем ціка́виться нови́нами, зокре́ма ви́борами.
example.source: Sam is interested in the news, the election in particular.

vocabulary.note: It introduces the same thing said again more exactly or in other words. A comma stands before it and none after it.

example.target: Він кана́дець, то́бто грома́дянин Кана́ди.
example.source: He is Canadian, that is, a citizen of Canada.

vocabulary.note: The predicative word 'ва́жливо' is formed from it. The superlative is 'найва́жливіший', the most important.

example.target: Для ме́не це ду́же ва́жливе пита́ння.
example.source: This is a very important question for me.
example.source_literal: For me this very important question.

vocabulary.note: With the genitive. It is 'у' with the locative of 'раз', here 'case', and after a vowel it is 'в ра́зі' by the euphony rule. Notices and instructions name a condition with it; speech uses 'якщо́' with a clause: 'якщо́ бу́де дощ'.

example.target: У ра́зі дощу́ конце́рт бу́де в музе́ї.
example.source: In case of rain, the concert will be in the museum.
example.source_literal: In case of-rain concert will-be in museum.

dialogues.title: What the headline means
dialogues.context: Taras now works in Lviv. Sam phones him from Kyiv because a headline about public transport, 'грома́дський тра́нспорт', puzzles him. 'Верхо́вна Ра́да', literally 'Supreme Council', is the parliament of Ukraine. Sam and Taras are friends and say 'ти' to each other.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: Тара́се, приві́т! Допоможи́ мені́, будь ла́ска. Я не розумі́ю оди́н заголо́вок.
lines.source: Hi, Taras! Help me, please. There's a headline I don't understand.
lines.source_literal: Taras, hi! Help to-me, please. I not understand one headline.

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: Приві́т! Прочита́й його́.
lines.source: Hi! Read it to me.
lines.source_literal: Hi! Read it.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: «Зако́н про грома́дський тра́нспорт ухва́лено». А хто його́ ухвали́в? Тут не ска́зано.
lines.source: 'Public transport law passed.' But who passed it? It doesn't say.
lines.source_literal: «Law about public transport passed». And who it passed? Here not said.

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: Його́ ухвали́ли депута́ти, то́бто Верхо́вна Ра́да. Зако́ни ухва́лює ті́льки вона́.
lines.source: The members of parliament passed it, that is, the Verkhovna Rada. Only the Rada passes laws.
lines.source_literal: It passed deputies, that-is Supreme Council. Laws passes only it.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: А чому́ не напи́сано: «Депута́ти ухвали́ли зако́н»?
lines.source: So why doesn't it say, 'The members of parliament passed the law'?
lines.source_literal: And why not written: «Deputies passed law»?

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: Так тако́ж мо́жна. Але́ в нови́нах ча́сто пи́шуть, що зро́блено, а не хто це зроби́в.
lines.source: You can write that too. But the news often says what has been done, not who did it.
lines.source_literal: So also possible. But in news often they-write, what done, and not who this did.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: Зрозумі́в. А в дру́гому ре́ченні є «відпові́дно до рефо́рми». Що це означа́є?
lines.source: Got it. And in the second sentence there's 'відпові́дно до рефо́рми'. What does that mean?
lines.source_literal: Understood. And in second sentence is «correspondingly to reform». What this means?

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: Це означа́є «так, як ка́же рефо́рма». У газе́тах так пи́шуть ча́сто.
lines.source: It means 'the way the reform says'. Newspapers often write like that.
lines.source_literal: This means «so, as says reform». In newspapers so they-write often.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: А тут ще одне́ ре́чення: «У зв’язку́ з рефо́рмою авто́буси ходи́тимуть ча́стіше». Це че́рез рефо́рму?
lines.source: And here's another sentence: 'In connection with the reform, buses will run more often.' Does that mean because of the reform?
lines.source_literal: And here still one sentence: «In connection with reform buses will-go more-often». This because-of reform?

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: Так, але́ «че́рез» ми ка́жемо про щось пога́не. А тут усе́ до́бре.
lines.source: Yes, but we say 'че́рез' about something bad. And here everything is good.
lines.source_literal: Yes, but «че́рез» we say about something bad. And here all good.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: Тоді́ мо́жна сказа́ти «завдяки́ рефо́рмі»?
lines.source: Then could you say 'thanks to the reform'?
lines.source_literal: Then possible to-say «thanks-to to-reform»?

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: Мо́жна. Але́ газе́та не ка́же, до́бре це чи пога́но. Тому́ вона́ пи́ше «у зв’язку́ з».
lines.source: You could. But a newspaper doesn't say whether it's good or bad. That's why it writes 'у зв’язку́ з'.
lines.source_literal: Possible. But newspaper not says, well this or badly. Therefore it writes «in connection with».

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: Ти до́бре поя́снюєш. Дя́кую, Тара́се!
lines.source: You explain things well. Thanks, Taras!
lines.source_literal: You well explain. I-thank, Taras!

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: Будь ла́ска. Коли́ я бу́ду в Ки́єві, почита́ємо нови́ни ра́зом.
lines.source: You're welcome. When I'm in Kyiv, we'll read some news together.
lines.source_literal: Please. When I will-be in Kyiv, we-will-read-a-while news together.

dialogues.title: A speech for the student council
dialogues.context: Oksana sits on the student council, 'студе́нтська ра́да', and tomorrow she gives a short speech, 'ви́ступ', at its meeting, 'засі́дання'. Her speech is a proposal, 'пропози́ція', a noun from 'пропонува́ти'. She rehearses it in front of Olena. The friends say 'ти' to each other, but the speech addresses the council with 'ви'. 'Запрацюва́ти', to start working, is 'працюва́ти' with the 'за-' that marks a start.

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: Оле́но, послу́хай мій ви́ступ, будь ла́ска. За́втра засі́дання студе́нтської ра́ди.
lines.source: Olena, please listen to my speech. The student council meets tomorrow.
lines.source_literal: Olena, listen my speech, please. Tomorrow meeting of-student of-council.

lines.speaker: Оле́на
lines.target: Дава́й, я слу́хаю. Ти бу́деш каза́ти ко́легам «ви»?
lines.source: Go ahead, I'm listening. Will you say 'ви' to the other members?
lines.source_literal: Let's, I listen. You will to-say to-colleagues «ви»?

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: Так, це ж засі́дання. Слу́хай: «Шано́вні ко́леги! Я ма́ю пропози́цію що́до ро́зкладу бібліоте́ки».
lines.source: Yes, it's a meeting, after all. Listen: 'Dear colleagues! I have a proposal regarding the library's opening hours.'
lines.source_literal: Yes, this after-all meeting. Listen: «Respected colleagues! I have proposal regarding timetable of-library».

lines.speaker: Оле́на
lines.target: Ого́, як у нови́нах! А яка́ пропози́ція?
lines.source: Wow, just like the news! So what's the proposal?
lines.source_literal: Wow, as in news! And what-kind proposal?

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: «Протя́гом тра́вня й че́рвня бібліоте́ка пови́нна працюва́ти до деся́тої ве́чора».
lines.source: 'During May and June, the library should be open until ten in the evening.'
lines.source_literal: «During May and June library obliged to-work until tenth of-evening».

lines.speaker: Оле́на
lines.target: А чому́ в тра́вні й че́рвні?
lines.source: And why in May and June?

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: «У зв’язку́ з і́спитами студе́нти бі́льше вча́ться, зокре́ма вве́чері».
lines.source: 'Because of the exams, students study more, especially in the evening.'
lines.source_literal: «In connection with exams students more study, in-particular in-evening».

lines.speaker: Оле́на
lines.target: До́бре. А хто бу́де працюва́ти в бібліоте́ці вве́чері?
lines.source: Good. And who will work in the library in the evening?
lines.source_literal: Good. And who will to-work in library in-evening?

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: «Я пропону́ю, щоб студе́нти самі́ бра́ли у́часть у робо́ті бібліоте́ки».
lines.source: 'I propose that the students themselves take part in running the library.'
lines.source_literal: «I propose, that-would students themselves took part in work of-library».

lines.speaker: Оле́на
lines.target: Це ціка́во. А з яко́го дня?
lines.source: That's interesting. And from what date?
lines.source_literal: This interesting. And from which day?

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: «У ра́зі зго́ди ра́ди нови́й ро́зклад запрацю́є з пе́ршого тра́вня».
lines.source: 'If the council agrees, the new hours will start on the first of May.'
lines.source_literal: «In case of-agreement of-council new timetable will-start-working from first of-May».

lines.speaker: Оле́на
lines.target: Ду́же до́бре. Ти говори́ш, як депута́тка!
lines.source: Very good. You sound like a member of parliament!
lines.source_literal: Very well. You speak, like deputy!

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: Сподіва́юся, що ра́да пого́диться.
lines.source: I hope the council agrees.
lines.source_literal: I-hope, that council will-agree.

lines.speaker: Оле́на
lines.target: Я ду́маю, що пого́диться. Твоя́ пропози́ція спра́вді ва́жлива.
lines.source: I think it will. Your proposal really is important.
lines.source_literal: I think, that will-agree. Your proposal really important.

grammar.title: Spelling and sound: стаття́, у зв’язку́, грома́дянин and the other new words
grammar.explanation:
'Стаття́' is written with a doubled 'тт', and by the rule of the third unit a doubled consonant letter is one long consonant: [stɑˈtʲːɑ]. The 'т' is soft before 'я', as in 'життя́'. The long consonant stands only before a vowel ending: 'статті́', 'статтю́', 'статте́ю'. The genitive plural has no ending, and there a single 'т' stands before 'е', where every Ukrainian consonant is hard: 'стате́й', [stɑˈtɛj]. The genitive plural of 'пита́ння' loses its doubled letter in the same way: 'пита́нь'. The verbal nouns of this unit, such as 'ухва́лення', adoption, 'обгово́рення', discussion, and 'відкриття́', opening, also have a long soft consonant before '-я'.

'Зв’язо́к', connection, has the apostrophe after 'в' before 'я'. As the third unit showed, the apostrophe after 'б', 'п', 'в', 'м', 'ф' and 'р' keeps the consonant hard and the [j] sounded: [zʋjɑˈzɔk]. The 'о' of the last syllable drops out in the other forms, so the locative is 'зв’язку́', [zʋjɑzˈku], and 'заголо́вок' gives 'заголо́вка' in the same way. In 'зв’язку́' the 'з' stays [z] before the voiceless 'к', since Ukrainian keeps a voiced consonant voiced. Before the group 'зв' the preposition takes the form 'у', as it does before 'св' and 'тв': 'у зв’язку́'.

'Грома́дянин' has four syllables, 'гро-ма́-дя-нин', and its stress stays on 'ма' in every form. The 'г' is [ɦ], and the 'д' is soft before 'я': [ɦrɔˈmɑdʲɑnɪn]. Nouns for people that end in '-янин' drop '-ин' in the plural: 'грома́дяни', genitive 'грома́дян'; 'кия́нин', a man from Kyiv, 'кия́ни'. The 'р' of 'уря́д' is soft before 'я' in the same way, and its final 'д' stays voiced: [uˈrʲɑd].

The other new words apply the rules of the opening units:

- 'Вла́да' begins with 'в' before a consonant, said [w]: [ˈwlɑdɑ].
- 'Ви́бори' is stressed on the prefix, like 'ви́брати', to choose, from which it comes. Its 'в' stands before a vowel and is [ʋ].
- 'У́часть' begins with a stressed 'у', which belongs to the noun and is not the preposition: 'бра́ти у́часть у ви́борах' has both.
- 'Згі́дно' begins with two voiced consonants, [zɦ]. 'Що́до' is one word that begins with 'щ', [ʃt͡ʃ].
- In 'то́бто' the 'б' stays voiced before 'т': [ˈtɔbtɔ].
- 'Ухвали́ти' is stressed on the ending in the 'я' form, 'ухвалю́', and on the stem in the others: 'ухва́лиш', 'ухва́лять'. The participle 'ухва́лений', the form 'ухва́лено' and the noun 'ухва́лення' keep the stem stress.
- 'Депута́т' and 'рефо́рма' came into Ukrainian from other languages, and their consonants before 'е' are hard, like every Ukrainian consonant there.

examples.target: Я прочита́в цю статтю́ вчо́ра.
examples.source: I read this article yesterday.

examples.target: У цій газе́ті бага́то стате́й.
examples.source: There are many articles in this newspaper.
examples.source_literal: In this newspaper many of-articles.

examples.target: У зв’язку́ з доще́м конце́рт перене́сено.
examples.source: Because of the rain, the concert has been moved.
examples.source_literal: In connection with rain concert moved.

examples.target: Заголо́вка ще нема́є.
examples.source: There's no headline yet.
examples.source_literal: Of-headline still there-is-not.

examples.target: Ми грома́дяни Украї́ни.
examples.source: We are citizens of Ukraine.
examples.source_literal: We citizens of-Ukraine.

grammar.title: Nominal style: verbal nouns in place of verbs
grammar.explanation:
Official texts and the news often name an action with a noun instead of a verb. It is the verbal noun taught in the unit on work: a neuter noun in '-ння' or '-ття' built from a verb, such as 'ухва́лення' from 'ухвали́ти', 'обгово́рення', discussion, from 'обговори́ти', to discuss, whose imperfective is 'обгово́рювати', and 'відкриття́' from 'відкри́ти'. Writing that carries its meaning in such nouns is called nominal style. It lets a whole action fit into a phrase that can follow a preposition or be the subject of a sentence, which a conjugated verb cannot do.

When a verb becomes a verbal noun, the words that depend on it change their form:

- The direct object goes into the genitive: 'ухвали́ти зако́н', to pass the law, gives 'ухва́лення зако́ну', the passing of the law.
- An adverb becomes an adjective that agrees with the noun: 'шви́дко ухвали́ти' gives 'шви́дке ухва́лення'.
- A phrase with a preposition stays as it is: 'повідо́мити про ви́бори' gives 'повідо́млення про ви́бори'.
- The doer, when it is named, goes into the instrumental, as with a passive participle: 'ухва́лення зако́ну депута́тами'. Most official texts leave it out.

Several such nouns in a row form a chain of genitives, each depending on the noun before it: 'пі́сля ухва́лення рефо́рми тра́нспорту', after the transport reform is adopted. Read the chain from the left, and find the verb inside each noun. Some nouns of official style end in '-ння' but are learned as words of their own, such as 'рі́шення', decision, related to 'ви́рішити', to decide. Others have no such ending and behave in the same way: 'ремо́нт мо́сту', the repair of the bridge.

Nominal style belongs to writing. In speech the verbal noun becomes a verb again, in a clause of its own: 'пі́сля ухва́лення зако́ну' is said 'коли́ зако́н ухвали́ли'. Ukrainian teachers of style advise writers to do the same on paper wherever the noun is not needed, because a text made only of nouns is hard to read. The last note of this unit shows the whole exchange.

grammar.title: Prepositions of official style: відпові́дно до, згі́дно з, у зв’язку́ з, з мето́ю, що́до
grammar.explanation:
Official Ukrainian has a set of compound prepositions: phrases of two or three words that work together as one preposition, and 'що́до', two words fused into one. Each was built from an ordinary word and a simple preposition or case form, and the last part decides the case that follows. Learn each with its case:

- 'відпові́дно до' with the genitive: in accordance with a rule, a law or a decision. 'Відпові́дно' is an adverb, correspondingly, from the root of 'ві́дповідь', and 'до' takes the genitive as always.
- 'згі́дно з' with the instrumental: according to a document or a plan. 'Згі́дно' means in agreement, and 'з' takes the instrumental, as in 'ка́ва з молоко́м'. It changes to 'із' or 'зі' by the euphony rule: 'згі́дно із зако́ном'.
- 'у зв’язку́ з' with the instrumental: in connection with, and in notices, because of. 'Зв’язо́к' is a connection.
- 'з мето́ю' with the genitive: for the purpose of. It is 'з' with the instrumental of 'мета́', goal, followed by the genitive of what the goal is.
- 'що́до' with the genitive: concerning, regarding. It names the topic of a question, an opinion or a decision.

English 'according to' has two kinds of Ukrainian equivalent, with different jobs. 'Згі́дно з' and 'відпові́дно до' cite a text or a plan: a law, a timetable, an order. A person's words are cited with 'за слова́ми' and the genitive, from the unit on reported speech: 'за слова́ми депута́та'.

'У зв’язку́ з' gives the cause of a change in a neutral, official way, whatever the result. Speech uses 'че́рез' with the accusative for a cause with a bad result and 'завдяки́' with the dative for one with a good result, as the unit on argument showed. A notice writes 'У зв’язку́ з ремо́нтом музе́й зачи́нено.', and a friend says 'Музе́й зачи́нений че́рез ремо́нт.'

Ukrainian punctuation does not require a comma after such a phrase at the start of a sentence: 'Відпові́дно до зако́ну ви́бори бу́дуть у жо́втні.'

grammar.title: The forms in '-но' and '-то' in official writing
grammar.explanation:
The unit on the passive taught the invariable forms in '-но' and '-то', which report a completed act without naming the doer: 'Музе́й відчи́нено.' Official texts and news reports use them far more often than speech does, because such texts state results: what has been decided, built, closed or adopted. Who did it is either clear from the context or beside the point.

The rules are the ones you know, now applied to the words of public life:

- The form never changes, and the sentence has no subject: 'Зако́н ухва́лено.' (The law has been passed.)
- What the action was done to stays in the accusative, so a feminine noun in '-а' takes '-у': 'Рефо́рму ухва́лено.', 'Статтю́ напи́сано.'
- On its own the form reports a completed act whose result counts now, also with a time word: 'Зако́н ухва́лено вчо́ра.' 'Було́', the neuter singular past of 'бу́ти', sets the act wholly in the past, and 'бу́де', its future form for 'він', 'вона́' and 'воно́', sets it in the future: 'Зако́н було́ ухва́лено в тра́вні.'

A form in '-но' or '-то' takes no doer. When the doer matters, the news names it as the subject of an active sentence with a perfective past, and this is the usual shape of a headline: 'Уря́д ухвали́в рефо́рму.' English headlines put such news in the present ('Government adopts reform'); Ukrainian keeps the past.

A passive participle describes a noun rather than reporting an act. After the noun it stands between commas together with the words that depend on it: 'Зако́н, ухва́лений учо́ра, ва́жливий для всіх.' (The law passed yesterday matters to everyone.)

In speech the 'вони́' form without 'вони́' does the work of the form in '-но': 'Зако́н ухвали́ли.' (They have passed the law.) It is the form to use when you retell an official text to a friend.

rows: The law was passed in May.
The reform will be adopted in the autumn.

examples.target: Зако́н про ви́бори ухва́лено.
examples.source: The election law has been passed.
examples.source_literal: Law about elections passed.

grammar.title: Parenthetical words, and clarifications with зокре́ма and то́бто
grammar.explanation:
The unit on argument taught that a parenthetical word comments on a sentence from outside and is set off by commas: one comma after it at the start of a sentence, one on each side in the middle, and one before it at the end. Formal writing and the news use many of them, mostly to say where a fact comes from or how it fits the text:

- 'як відо́мо', literally 'as known': as is well known, for a fact the writer takes as shared
- 'за слова́ми' with the genitive: according to someone
- 'напри́клад': for example
- 'по-пе́рше', 'по-дру́ге': firstly, secondly
- 'на жаль': unfortunately
- 'о́тже': so, when it opens a conclusion

A test shows whether a word is parenthetical: remove it, and the sentence is still complete and correct. 'Зако́н, як відо́мо, ва́жливий.' becomes 'Зако́н ва́жливий.'

'Зокре́ма' and 'то́бто' can look like parenthetical words, but they are not. 'Зокре́ма' is an adverb, in particular, and 'то́бто' is a conjunction, that is. Each introduces a clarification: a part of the sentence that names more exactly something said just before it. 'Зокре́ма' picks one member out of a group ('для всіх, зокре́ма для студе́нтів'), and 'то́бто' says the same thing again in other words ('у жо́втні, то́бто восени́'). The clarification belongs to the grammar of the sentence, so its punctuation differs from that of a parenthetical word:

- A comma stands before 'зокре́ма' or 'то́бто'.
- No comma follows them.
- If the sentence goes on after the clarification, a comma closes it: 'Мої́ дру́зі, зокре́ма Окса́на, ча́сто чита́ють нови́ни.'

These commas belong to writing. A reader reading aloud makes at most a short pause at each of them.

rows: На жаль, зако́н ще не ухва́лено.

grammar.title: Standard forms of formal writing: бра́ти у́часть, протя́гом, у ра́зі
grammar.explanation:
Formal writing and careful public speech keep to the standard forms of the language, and the editors of newspapers and official texts check for them. Three that almost every official text needs are worth learning as fixed units, each with its case:

- 'бра́ти у́часть у' with the locative: to take part in. 'Бра́ти' changes as usual ('беру́', 'бере́ш', 'брав'), while the noun 'у́часть', participation, never changes. For one completed act use the perfective, 'взя́ти у́часть'. Without the verb, 'у́часть у ви́борах' means participation in the election.
- 'протя́гом' with the genitive: during, over a period, from the unit on narration. It stresses that something fills the whole period: 'протя́гом ти́жня', 'протя́гом двох ро́ків'. Official texts use it for the time a rule or a change lasts.
- 'у ра́зі' with the genitive: in case of. It is 'у' with the locative of 'раз', here 'case', and after a vowel it becomes 'в ра́зі' by the euphony rule. It names a condition with a noun: 'у ра́зі дощу́', in case of rain; 'у ра́зі потре́би', if necessary, from 'потре́ба', need.

When the condition is a whole clause rather than a noun, Ukrainian uses 'якщо́': 'Якщо́ бу́де дощ, конце́рт бу́де в музе́ї.' The noun after 'у ра́зі' is often a verbal noun, which is why this preposition belongs to the nominal style of the earlier note.

rows: to take part in the election
to take part in the election

examples.source: Over the year, the government adopted three reforms.
examples.source_literal: During year government adopted three reforms.

examples.source: If you have a cold, you need to drink a lot of water.

examples.source_literal: Sam took part in concert.

grammar.title: From official text to plain words, and back
grammar.explanation:
A Ukrainian reader meets official style in notices, in letters from institutions and in the news, and often retells it to someone in plain words. A learner also needs the reverse: to write a short formal summary or report. Both are the same set of exchanges, made in opposite directions.

To retell an official text in plain words:

- Turn each verbal noun back into a verb with a clause of its own: 'пі́сля ухва́лення зако́ну' becomes 'коли́ зако́н ухвали́ли'.
- Replace each preposition of official style with the word of speech: 'у зв’язку́ з' with 'че́рез', 'з мето́ю' with 'щоб', 'що́до' with 'про', 'відпові́дно до' with 'за' and the instrumental ('за зако́ном', under the law), 'у ра́зі' with 'якщо́'.
- Turn a form in '-но' or '-то' into the 'вони́' form, or name the doer: 'Зако́н ухва́лено.' becomes 'Зако́н ухвали́ли.'
- Keep every fact: dates, places, numbers and names.

To write a formal summary, make the same exchanges the other way, and keep to the habits of formal writing:

- Name the source first: 'Відпові́дно до оголо́шення...', 'За слова́ми...'.
- Report results with forms in '-но' and '-то' or with the institution as the subject, and leave out your own opinion.
- Use the standard forms of the previous note and the commas of parenthetical words.
- Address readers with 'ви', and open a report to a group with 'Шано́вні ко́леги!' or 'Шано́вні грома́дяни!'.

Do not exchange every phrase: a summary made only of verbal nouns is as hard to read as the text it summarizes.

examples.target: Че́рез ремо́нт міст бу́де закри́тий усе́ лі́то.

examples.source_literal: Because-of repair bridge will-be closed all summer.

examples.target: Коли́ зако́н ухвали́ли, квитки́ ста́ли деше́вшими.

examples.source_literal: When law they-passed, tickets became by-cheaper.

examples.source: If it rains, the concert will be in the museum.
examples.source_literal: If will-be rain, concert will-be in museum.

culture.title: The official style, the press and the institutions in the news
culture.text:
Ukrainian grammar describes several styles of the written language, each with its own choice of words and constructions. Two of them fill the texts this unit prepares you to read:

- 'офіці́йно-ділови́й стиль', literally 'official-business style': laws, decrees, notices, applications and formal letters
- 'публіцисти́чний стиль', the style of writing on public affairs: newspapers, news sites and political speeches

The official style aims at a single meaning that no reader can dispute. It repeats a noun rather than replace it with a pronoun, and it relies on verbal nouns, forms in '-но' and '-то' and fixed phrases such as 'відпові́дно до'. The style of the press borrows these, but it also wants to be read, so its headlines are short active sentences such as 'Ра́да ухвали́ла зако́н', and its reports name the source of every claim. Ukrainian teachers of style warn against texts that pile up verbal nouns, and advise the plain verb wherever it says the same thing.

These are the institutions that the news names most often:

- 'Верхо́вна Ра́да', literally 'Supreme Council': the parliament and the only body that passes laws, with 450 'наро́дні депута́ти', literally 'people's deputies', elected for five years
- 'Кабіне́т Міні́стрів', the Cabinet of Ministers, which is what 'уря́д', government, names
- 'президе́нт', the president, elected for five years, who signs the laws that the Rada passes
- 'грома́да', community: since 2020 the whole country has been divided into territorial communities, each with its own elected council, also called 'ра́да'

The word 'ра́да' shares its root with 'ра́дити', to advise: a council is a body that deliberates and advises. 'Грома́да' gives 'грома́дянин', citizen, and 'грома́дський', public, as in 'грома́дський тра́нспорт'. The public broadcaster of Ukraine, created in 2017 in place of the former state television and radio, is called 'Суспі́льне', literally 'the public one', from 'суспі́льство', society.

paragraphs.target: Верхо́вна Ра́да ухвали́ла нови́й зако́н про грома́дський тра́нспорт. Зако́н ухва́лено вчо́ра пі́сля до́вгого обгово́рення.
paragraphs.source: The Verkhovna Rada has passed a new law on public transport. The law was passed yesterday after a long debate.
paragraphs.source_literal: Supreme Council passed new law about public transport. Law passed yesterday after long discussion.

paragraphs.target: Відпові́дно до зако́ну в ко́жному мі́сті бу́де оди́н квито́к для авто́буса й метро́. Його́ мо́жна бу́де купи́ти че́рез телефо́н.
paragraphs.source: Under the law, every city will have one ticket for the bus and the metro. It will be possible to buy it on a phone.
paragraphs.source_literal: Correspondingly to law in every city will-be one ticket for bus and metro. It possible will-be to-buy through phone.

paragraphs.target: Протя́гом двох ро́ків міста́ пови́нні купи́ти нові́ ти́хі авто́буси. У ра́зі потре́би уря́д дасть міста́м гро́ші.
paragraphs.source: Within two years, cities must buy new, quiet buses. If necessary, the government will give the cities money.
paragraphs.source_literal: During two years cities obliged to-buy new quiet buses. In case of-need government will-give to-cities money.

paragraphs.target: Найбі́льше пита́нь у грома́дян що́до ціни́ квитка́. За слова́ми депута́та Іва́на Петре́нка, квито́к не бу́де доро́жчим.
paragraphs.source: Citizens have the most questions about the price of the ticket. According to Ivan Petrenko, a member of parliament, the ticket will not cost more.
paragraphs.source_literal: Most of-questions at citizens regarding price of-ticket. By words of-deputy Ivan Petrenko, ticket not will-be by-more-expensive.

paragraphs.target: Нови́й квито́к запрацю́є з пе́ршого сі́чня, то́бто з поча́тку ро́ку.
paragraphs.source: The new ticket will come into use on the first of January, that is, at the start of the year.
paragraphs.source_literal: New ticket will-start-working from first of-January, that-is from beginning of-year.

paragraphs.target: Зако́н обгово́рювали протя́гом трьох мі́сяців. В обгово́ренні взяли́ у́часть депута́ти й грома́дяни, зокре́ма студе́нти.
paragraphs.source: The law was debated for three months. Members of parliament and citizens, students in particular, took part in the debate.
paragraphs.source_literal: Law they-discussed during three months. In discussion took part deputies and citizens, in-particular students.

questions.prompt: Under the new law, what will every city have?
choices: One ticket for the bus and the metro
questions.explanation: 'Відпові́дно до зако́ну в ко́жному мі́сті бу́де оди́н квито́к для авто́буса й метро́.'

questions.prompt: When will the government give the cities money?
questions.explanation: 'У ра́зі потре́би', literally 'in case of need', names a condition: the government will pay only if the cities need it.

questions.prompt: What did Ivan Petrenko say about the ticket?
choices: It can only be bought on a phone.
questions.explanation: 'За слова́ми депута́та Іва́на Петре́нка, квито́к не бу́де доро́жчим.' 'За слова́ми' cites a person, and 'доро́жчий' is the comparative of 'дороги́й'.

questions.prompt: Why does the report write 'Зако́н ухва́лено вчо́ра' without naming who passed the law?
choices: Nobody knows who passed the law.
The law has not been passed yet.
The first sentence has already named the Verkhovna Rada, and a news report states the result with the form in '-но'.
questions.explanation: A form in '-но' reports the result and takes no doer. The doer is already clear from 'Верхо́вна Ра́да ухвали́ла...'.

questions.prompt: Who took part in the debate on the law?
choices: Members of parliament and citizens, including students
questions.explanation: 'В обгово́ренні взяли́ у́часть депута́ти й грома́дяни, зокре́ма студе́нти.' 'Зокре́ма' picks the students out of the citizens.

paragraphs.target: Шано́вні грома́дяни! Відпові́дно до рі́шення міської́ ра́ди міст че́рез рі́чку бу́де закри́то протя́гом ли́пня й се́рпня.
paragraphs.source: Dear citizens! In accordance with the decision of the city council, the bridge over the river will be closed during July and August.
paragraphs.source_literal: Respected citizens! Correspondingly to decision of-city of-council bridge across river will-be closed during July and August.

paragraphs.target: У зв’язку́ з ремо́нтом мо́сту авто́буси ходи́тимуть че́рез центр мі́ста. Зупи́нку бі́ля мо́сту перене́сено на пло́щу.
paragraphs.source: Due to the repairs on the bridge, buses will run through the city center. The stop near the bridge has been moved to the square.
paragraphs.source_literal: In connection with repair of-bridge buses will-go through center of-city. Stop near bridge moved on square.

paragraphs.target: У ра́зі пита́нь що́до ро́зкладу авто́бусів про́симо писа́ти до міської́ ра́ди. Дя́куємо за розумі́ння.
paragraphs.source: If you have questions about the bus timetable, please write to the city council. Thank you for your understanding.
paragraphs.source_literal: In case of-questions regarding timetable of-buses we-ask to-write to city council. We-thank for understanding.

paragraphs.target: Що це означа́є? Міст бу́дуть ремонтува́ти все лі́то, тому́ він бу́де закри́тий.
paragraphs.source: What does this mean? They will be repairing the bridge all summer, so it will be closed.
paragraphs.source_literal: What this means? Bridge they-will to-repair all summer, so it will-be closed.

paragraphs.target: Авто́буси ходи́тимуть че́рез центр, а зупи́нка бу́де на пло́щі. Якщо́ ма́єте пита́ння, напиші́ть до ра́ди.
paragraphs.source: The buses will run through the center, and the stop will be on the square. If you have questions, write to the council.
paragraphs.source_literal: Buses will-go through center, and stop will-be on square. If you-have questions, write to council.

questions.prompt: Why will the bridge be closed?
questions.explanation: 'У зв’язку́ з ремо́нтом мо́сту', due to the repairs on the bridge, and the summary says 'Міст бу́дуть ремонтува́ти'.

questions.prompt: When will the bridge be closed?
questions.explanation: 'Протя́гом ли́пня й се́рпня': 'протя́гом' with the genitive names the whole period.

questions.prompt: Where is the bus stop during the repairs?
questions.explanation: 'Зупи́нку бі́ля мо́сту перене́сено на пло́щу', and the summary says 'зупи́нка бу́де на пло́щі'.

questions.prompt: Which words of the notice does the plain summary retell as 'Якщо́ ма́єте пита́ння'?
questions.explanation: 'У ра́зі' with the genitive names a condition with a noun; speech says the same with 'якщо́' and a clause.

questions.prompt: The notice says 'Зупи́нку бі́ля мо́сту перене́сено на пло́щу.' What does this sentence leave unsaid?
choices: Whether the stop has been moved
questions.explanation: A form in '-но' reports a completed act and its result, and it never names the doer.

exercises.prompt: Match the Ukrainian words with their meanings
Match the prepositions of official style with their meanings

choices: The members of parliament adopted the reform.

exercises.prompt: Which word names the people who hold power in a city or a country?
exercises.explanation: 'Вла́да' is power and the people who hold it: 'міська́ вла́да', the city authorities. It is singular in Ukrainian.

choices: The election will be in November.
The election will be in October.
The election will be in December.

exercises.prompt: 'Ці ви́бори бу́ли ду́же ва́жливі.' Why are the verb and the adjective plural when there was one election?
exercises.explanation: 'Ви́бори' has no singular in this meaning, so its verb and adjectives are always plural. 'Ви́бір', choice, is a different word.
Nouns for people in '-янин' drop '-ин' in the plural: 'грома́дяни', 'кия́ни'. 'Грома́дянина' is the genitive singular.

exercises.audio_target: У зв’язку́ з ви́борами шко́лу зачи́нено.
choices: Due to the election, the school is open.
Due to the repairs, the school is closed.
Due to the election, the school is closed.

exercises.hint_source: The members of parliament adopted the reform yesterday.
exercises.explanation: The past of the perfective 'ухвали́ти' agrees with the plural subject 'депута́ти': 'ухвали́ли'.
A form in '-но' has no subject, and what the action was done to stays in the accusative: 'рефо́рма' becomes 'рефо́рму'.

exercises.prompt_target: Відпові́дно ___ ро́зкладу авто́бус приї́де о сьо́мій.
exercises.hint_source: According to the timetable, the bus will arrive at seven.
exercises.explanation: 'Відпові́дно до' is one compound preposition, and 'до' takes the genitive: 'ро́зкладу'.

exercises.audio_target: У ра́зі дощу́ зу́стріч бу́де в бібліоте́ці.
choices: In case of rain, the meeting will be in the library.
In case of rain, the meeting will be in the museum.
After the rain, the meeting will be in the library.

exercises.hint_source: The council works in line with the law.
exercises.explanation: 'Згі́дно з' takes the instrumental, and before 'з' the preposition becomes 'із' by the euphony rule: 'згі́дно із зако́ном'.

exercises.hint_source: The bridge is closed due to repairs.
exercises.explanation: 'У зв’язку́ з' ends in 'з', which takes the instrumental: 'ремо́нт' becomes 'ремо́нтом'.

exercises.hint_source: I have a question about the article.
exercises.explanation: 'Що́до' takes the genitive. The genitive of 'стаття́' is 'статті́', with the doubled 'тт' before the ending vowel.

exercises.hint_source: My parents took part in the election.
exercises.explanation: 'Бра́ти у́часть' changes only its verb. The perfective 'взяли́' reports one completed act; the imperfective 'бра́ли' presents it as a fact or a habit.

exercises.hint_source: We worked on the article for a week.
exercises.explanation: 'Протя́гом' with the genitive says that the work filled the whole week.

exercises.prompt_target: Ми прийде́мо о сьо́мій, ___ пі́сля робо́ти.
exercises.hint_source: We'll come at seven, that is, after work.
exercises.explanation: 'То́бто' says the same thing again in other words. A comma stands before it and none after it.

exercises.hint_source: We are waiting for the bridge to open.
exercises.explanation: The verbal noun of 'відкри́ти' ends in '-ття', as its participle 'відкри́тий' ends in '-тий'. Its object follows in the genitive: 'мо́сту'.

exercises.hint_source: The new law was passed yesterday.
Sam read the headline of the article.
The citizens took part in the election.

exercises.prompt: 'Зако́н ухва́лено.' Who passed the law, according to this sentence?
exercises.explanation: A form in '-но' reports a completed act and its result and never names the doer. Only an active sentence such as 'Ра́да ухвали́ла зако́н' names it.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase is the verbal noun version of 'ухвали́ти зако́н'?
exercises.explanation: The verbal noun 'ухва́лення' takes the object of the verb in the genitive: 'зако́ну'. 'Ухва́лений зако́н' is a participle describing the law, and 'ухва́лено' is the form in '-но'.

exercises.prompt: A notice says 'у зв’язку́ з ремо́нтом'. Which preposition does everyday speech use for a cause like this, with an unwelcome result?
exercises.explanation: 'Че́рез ремо́нт' names a cause with a bad result. 'Завдяки́' is for a cause with a good result, and 'що́до' names a topic, not a cause.

exercises.prompt: Which is the everyday equivalent of 'з мето́ю навча́ння'?
exercises.explanation: 'З мето́ю' names a purpose, which speech gives with 'щоб' and an infinitive. 'Пі́сля' means after, and 'що́до' means regarding.

exercises.prompt: In 'Ви́бори, як відо́мо, бу́дуть восени́.', why does a comma stand on each side of 'як відо́мо'?
choices: It is a parenthetical phrase in the middle of the sentence.
It is the subject of the sentence.
exercises.explanation: 'Як відо́мо' comments on the sentence from outside: without it, 'Ви́бори бу́дуть восени́.' is still complete. A parenthetical word in the middle takes a comma on each side.

exercises.prompt: In 'Нови́й зако́н ва́жливий для всіх, зокре́ма для студе́нтів.', why is there no comma after 'зокре́ма'?
choices: Because 'зокре́ма' introduces a clarification that belongs to the sentence, so only a comma before it is written
Because Ukrainian never writes a comma after an adverb
Because the sentence is too short for a second comma
exercises.explanation: 'Зокре́ма' is not a parenthetical word. It opens a clarification, which takes a comma before it and, if the sentence goes on, a comma after the whole clarification.

exercises.prompt: Why is the 'т' doubled in 'стаття́' but single in 'стате́й'?
choices: The doubled letter shows the stress.
The long consonant stands only before a vowel ending, and the genitive plural 'стате́й' has no ending.
exercises.explanation: The doubled 'тт' is one long soft consonant that needs a vowel ending after it, as in 'статті́' and 'статтю́'. 'Пита́ння' loses its doubled letter in 'пита́нь' in the same way.

exercises.prompt: Why is there an apostrophe in 'зв’язо́к'?
choices: After 'в' before 'я' it keeps 'в' hard and the [j] sounded.
exercises.explanation: After 'б', 'п', 'в', 'м', 'ф' and 'р' before 'я', 'ю', 'є' or 'ї', the apostrophe keeps the consonant hard and the [j] sounded: [zʋjɑˈzɔk].

exercises.prompt: In the first dialogue, why does the headline not say who passed the law, according to Taras?
choices: Because the members of parliament asked the newspaper not to name them
Because the news often says what has been done, not who did it
Because the government passed the law
exercises.explanation: 'Але́ в нови́нах ча́сто пи́шуть, що зро́блено, а не хто це зроби́в.' Taras adds that only the Verkhovna Rada passes laws.

exercises.prompt: In the second dialogue, what does Oksana propose to the student council?
choices: That the library stay open until ten in the evening in May and June
That the library close in May and June
That the exams move to June
exercises.explanation: 'Протя́гом тра́вня й че́рвня бібліоте́ка пови́нна працюва́ти до деся́тої ве́чора', because students study more during the exams.

exercises.prompt_source: The reform was adopted in May.
Oksana has a proposal regarding the timetable.
Due to the exams, the library is open until ten.
The election will be in October, that is, in the autumn.
The new timetable has been adopted.
exercises.explanation: Official texts and the news use the form in '-но'; speech uses the 'вони́' form without 'вони́'.

exercises.prompt_source: The law will be passed in the spring.
exercises.explanation: 'Бу́де' places the form in '-но' in the future, and 'ухва́лять', the 'вони́' form of the perfective, says the same in speech.

exercises.prompt_source: Sam took part in the election.
exercises.explanation: After the consonant at the end of 'Сем', euphony gives 'узя́в'. The event follows 'у' with the locative: 'у ви́борах'.

exercises.prompt_source: Due to the rain, the concert will be in the museum.
answers: У зв’язку́ з доще́м конце́рт бу́де в музе́ї.
Че́рез дощ конце́рт бу́де в музе́ї.
Конце́рт бу́де в музе́ї че́рез дощ.
exercises.explanation: 'У зв’язку́ з' takes the instrumental, 'доще́м', in an official notice; in speech 'че́рез' takes the accusative, 'дощ'.
